acceptance_criteria.criterion: ErrorResponse::makeForbidden() returns self and sets the HTTP status code to 403.
makeForbidden() follows the same one-liner pattern as makeBadRequest() and makeInternalServerError().
PHPStan analysis passes without regressions on the framework.

summary: Added ERROR_METHOD_NOT_GRANTED (183005) and ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_RIGHTS (183006) constants to APIMethodInterface following the existing 183000-range sequential numbering.

Added makeForbidden() to ErrorResponse as a one-liner delegating to setHTTPStatusCode(Connectors_ResponseCode::HTTP_FORBIDDEN), following the same pattern as makeBadRequest() and makeInternalServerError().
PHPStan analysis passes with zero errors (2141 files analysed).

comments.note: No observations — code in the touched files is clean and consistent. The ErrorResponse builder pattern (setHTTPStatusCode one-liners) is well-established and makeForbidden() slots in without any friction.

summary: All five acceptance criteria verified by direct source inspection and test execution. Both new constants (ERROR_METHOD_NOT_GRANTED=183005, ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_RIGHTS=183006) are present in APIMethodInterface with correct sequential values and no duplicates in the 183xxx range. makeForbidden() is a one-liner following the identical pattern to makeBadRequest() and makeInternalServerError(), correctly delegating to setHTTPStatusCode(Connectors_ResponseCode::HTTP_FORBIDDEN) where HTTP_FORBIDDEN=403. PHPStan passes cleanly at 2141 files. Existing ErrorResponse and APIMethod tests pass without regressions.

comments.note: No observations — all implementations are clean and consistent. Constants are correctly typed (const int), sequentially numbered without gaps, and the makeForbidden() one-liner is identical in structure to its siblings. No edge-case risk identified.

summary: WP-001 passes code review. Two new constants (ERROR_METHOD_NOT_GRANTED=183005, ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_RIGHTS=183006) are correctly typed, sequentially numbered, and placed on the canonical APIMethodInterface. makeForbidden() follows the identical one-liner pattern as its siblings (makeBadRequest, makeInternalServerError) — delegating to setHTTPStatusCode(Connectors_ResponseCode::HTTP_FORBIDDEN=403) and returning self. No Fix-Forward changes applied. One Documentation-Forward note raised for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: The semantic split between ERROR_METHOD_NOT_GRANTED and ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_RIGHTS is currently undocumented. Both describe access-denied scenarios, and downstream callers in WP-003/WP-005 need a clear rule for which to use in which situation. This is not a blocker at WP-001 scope (the constants are merely declared here), but the distinction should be captured in docblocks before WP-003 lands.

[documentation-forward] APIMethodDetailTmpl.php::resolveHTTPStatusCodes() hardcodes only HTTP 200, 400, and 500 in the documentation UI status-code list. Now that makeForbidden() exists as a first-class builder, HTTP 403 should appear in that list with an appropriate description (e.g. 'Forbidden — insufficient rights to call this method'). WP-004 addresses OpenAPI 403 documentation; ensure this UI template is also updated as part of that work or a follow-up Documentation task.

summary: Added docblocks to ERROR_METHOD_NOT_GRANTED and ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_RIGHTS in APIMethodInterface clarifying their semantic distinction: 183005 signals a method-level grant failure (key not whitelisted for the endpoint); 183006 signals a rights-level failure (key has method access but user lacks the required right). Both docblocks include @see cross-references to makeForbidden().
Added docblock to ErrorResponse::makeForbidden() explaining it sets HTTP 403, when to use it (authorization failures), and linking back to both error constants.

Updated src/classes/Application/API/README.md Key Concepts section: added Authorization entry documenting ERROR_METHOD_NOT_GRANTED, ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_RIGHTS, and makeForbidden() in the module overview.

Acknowledged documentation-forward note about APIMethodDetailTmpl.php::resolveHTTPStatusCodes() — HTTP 403 addition is deferred to WP-004 (OpenAPI 403 Response Documentation) as specified by the reviewer.

comments.note: Docblocks on the two new constants use @see cross-references to makeForbidden(), creating bidirectional discoverability between the error constants and the response builder method.
